title: aggregator(saas-extract): six text caps split surrogate pairs — reads/conflicts/PAYG/usage/metric notes raw-slice at 400/300/220/600, bypassing the #7694 capUnits guard

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Something isn't working (prefixed form of the classic bug label)

labels.name: task/small-fix
labels.description: Queue packet kind: bounded fix with reproduction and targeted tests

body:
## Summary

`saas-extract.ts` caps six extracted text fields with raw UTF-16 slices. When an astral character straddles a cap, the field ends in a lone high surrogate; `JSON.stringify` stores it as the `\ud83d` escape and a UTF-8 encode/decode round-trip (the feed/board JSON is written to disk and re-read) replaces it with U+FFFD. Same defect class as #7694/#7711/#7725/#7731/#7736 — in the SaaS extractor, which none of those fixes covered. #7741 (filed today for the three 240-char diagnostic caps) states the other remaining slices in `pm-stack/aggregator/src` are "dates/hex/slugs over ASCII-safe alphabets, or the event writers already tracked in #7740" — that audit missed this module: its inputs are quota-view prose and collector-export detail strings, not ASCII-safe alphabets.

## Evidence

Raw slice sites (main `752357c139ba`):

- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/saas-extract.ts:84` — `readsOf`: dated-read text `line.slice(0, 400)` (line is quota-view prose)
- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/saas-extract.ts:94` — `conflictsOf`: conflict line `line.slice(0, 400)`
- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/saas-extract.ts:119` — `paygOf`: PAYG estimate note `.slice(0, 300)`
- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/saas-extract.ts:130` — `paygOf`: not-applicable note `` `not applicable — ${why}`.slice(0, 220) ``
- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/saas-extract.ts:744` — `extractSaasServices`: `usageNote: usageText.slice(0, 600)` (the section's Usage/dates bullet)
- `pm-stack/aggregator/src/saas-extract.ts:1065` — `applySupabaseExport`: metric `note: parts.join(" ").slice(0, 600)` (parts include the export doc's `live.detail`)

The outputs are `SaasService` fields (`reads[].text`, `conflicts[]`, `paygEstimate.note`, `paygNote`, `usageNote`, `metrics[].note`) — carried into the aggregator's feed/board JSON and rendered on the quota/SaaS cards.

## Verification (this run, laptop primary @ `752357c139ba`)

Probes `~/git/fleet/probe-saas-surrogate/probe.ts`, `probe2.ts`, `probe3.ts` (laptop), importing the real `extractSaasServices` / `applySupabaseExport` (module md5 `4c64892a6f09c1a5e6973cb4b322efb7`). Each input places U+1F600 straddling the cap; controls place the pair ending exactly at the cap:

```
straddle reads[0]     | len: 400 | lone: true  | utf8-rt changes: true
straddle conflicts[0] | len: 400 | lone: true  | utf8-rt changes: true
straddle payg.note    | len: 300 | lone: true  | utf8-rt changes: true
straddle paygNote     | len: 220 | lone: true  | (stored value ends in \ud83d)
straddle usageNote    | len: 600 | lone: true  | utf8-rt changes: true
straddle metric note  | len: 600 | lone: true  | utf8-rt changes: true
control reads[0]      | len: 400 | lone: false | utf8-rt changes: false
control metric note   | len: 600 | lone: false | utf8-rt changes: false
json stored contains lone escape: true
```

Every straddle case ends in a lone `\ud83d`; exact-fit controls are intact, so this is the cut, not the inputs.

## Why it matters

These fields exist to be read when reconciling subscriptions and usage: dated reads, recorded conflicts between sources, PAYG estimate notes, and live-export metric detail. Corrupting the tail of exactly the longest entries hides the end of the record — and puts lone-surrogate escapes into the shared feed JSON other consumers parse. Same fix shape as the six merged predecessors: a pair straddling the cap is dropped whole.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] No text cap in `saas-extract.ts` (400/300/220/600 sites above) can return a string ending in a lone surrogate: a pair straddling the cap is dropped whole (result is cap−1 units), mirroring the `capUnits` semantics of #7694.
- [ ] Exact-fit strings (pair ending exactly at the cap) and under-cap strings pass through unchanged; all other extraction behaviour is unchanged.
- [ ] Regression tests pin the straddle cases (fail on the pre-fix code) and the exact-fit controls for the capped fields.
- [ ] Existing aggregator suites that exercise this module (e.g. `supabase-export.test.ts`, `cloudflare-export.test.ts`, `charges-catalog.test.ts`) still pass.
